title: Underground Lake
text: “That’s the thing, isn’t it. Even Gaelion-chan doesn’t seem to fully understand it, and apparently there are gaps in her memory during the loops too—not as bad as Motoyasu-kun’s, but still. Maybe the mystery lies somewhere in that.”
“If we got hold of a similar weapon, it might be possible, but according to Gaelion-san, even she couldn’t manage it.”
“Either way, sounds like it’s beyond us.”

“Still, even if looping itself isn’t possible for us, I’ll be honest—I do want to do something about the other looping versions of myself. Specifically, something other than killing them or having Fleon-san brainwash them.”
“Same here. I’d like to wake them up to the truth as early as possible, the way we were.”
“Easier said than done, though… it’s not like we get sent right after the summoning like before…”
More often than not, it happens partway through a loop, I say.
“Ren-san, instead of just relying on Motoyasu-san, wouldn’t it be worthwhile for us to do some research of our own?”
“That’s true, but…”
“As for me, I’d like to save Father while also meeting Filo-tan, indeed.”
Come to think of it, there had never been a case where both a gentle Father and Filo-tan coexisted, I say. Whenever Filo-tan was present, Father seemed to bear some emotional wound, indeed.
“So the challenge is getting the current Naofumi and Filo to coexist.”
“I think the conditions there are pretty clear, since we heard them from Gaelion-chan.”
What!? Does Father know a way for both Filo-tan and saving Father to coexist!?
“Please tell me, I say!”

“There’s a lot to consider there, and we need to organize the information first. Let’s save it for after this incident’s over. Otherwise we might not be able to focus on the fight and end up overlooking something important.”
“That’s true. It does sound like something requiring careful organization. And for our own future research, first priority should be returning to normal.”
“Yeah, I’d rather not stay like this for the rest of my life.”

And so, talking amongst ourselves, we pressed steadily onward, I say. Along the way, we came across quite a few treasure chests here and there, I say. There didn’t seem to be any traps, and they opened easily enough.
“So… we just keep popping open every treasure we find, but is it really okay that there are no traps?”
“That falls under the weapons’ appraisal skills. They can detect traps and curses.”
“Convenient, I suppose. Though if I had to guess who’d be best at disarming traps among us, it’d be Itsuki.”
“In a classic RPG, the bow would go to the ranger or thief type, and I’m the one with the weapon that fits that role. Makes sense given the emphasis on dexterity.”
“In practice though, it’s more like all of us can sense traps just by relying on our weapons.”
“Only if the corresponding weapon or skill level is high enough, though.”
“Even then, we’re still inferior to actual specialists—like Lars-chan, who’s great at lockpicking and trap disposal.”

Panda was quite skilled in that area, I say. Older Sister also seemed to have a good sense for detecting traps, indeed. Apparently she could tell via echolocation—makes sense, being an orca beastwoman.
“They’re multi-talented, aren’t they. Both of Naofumi-san’s wives.”
“Yeah.”

“Well, Lars-san says she has no interest in cooking herself, but she makes baby food whenever I’m not around, and apparently, according to her subordinates, she can casually handle a huge wok and stir-fry things like nothing.”

She never does any of that in front of Father, though—so it seems Panda can actually do such things, I say. It reminded me of the time Father used a massive Chinese wok to make fried rice during a cooking contest against Ren. That sweeping motion, moving the whole pan without spilling a single grain—now that was a sight to behold, I say.
“Sadeena-san apparently does her own cooking too, and can do a bit of everything—dexterous, if you want to call it that. She made us a meal the other day.”
“Probably just something to go with drinks, knowing her.”
“Ahaha… but honestly, I think Rishia-san’s the best when it comes to appraising and researching objects. She’s incredibly knowledgeable.”
“True. We tend to rely on our weapons for appraisal, but Rishia-san can often tell just by looking.”
“The old man at the weapon shop’s good at that too, but only for weapons.”

By the way, according to Ren, he’d apparently used the weapon shop old man’s storeroom to hide away various things he’d acquired from the world of dark cuisine, I say. Bringing in such odd items… and apparently his kitchen knives had even been spotted and sharpened for him there, indeed.
“Rishia-san’s grades at school were terrifyingly good, you know. Even looking at her past exam records.”
“I believe it, but that’s the same school Takt and that princess attended, right?”
“Yes. Takt apparently did all sorts of things and ranked among the best in the school’s history, but as for that princess—her actual grades weren’t anything to write home about.”
“Figures. Not to speak ill, but going by what Motoyasu and Gaelion say about her, she sounds like a real piece of work. It’d be more surprising if her grades had been good.”
“And Melty-chan’s so smart, too.”

There was no comparison to be made between the Crimson Swine and Fiancée’s intelligence, I say. Fiancée was surely thousands of times sharper. Though when it came to scheming and plotting, the Crimson Swine’s marks were probably quite high indeed.
“What we do know is that even the instructors and combat trainers who were strict with that princess apparently saw no real improvement in her.”
“Makes you wonder what that woman was even doing with her time…”
“Conspiracies and scheming require some intelligence, don’t they. Maybe her cunning was reserved solely for underhanded plots.”

That’s just how pigs are, I say. On top of that, they’re creatures who preach equality between men and women while never complaining when they themselves are the ones benefiting from favoritism, indeed. No doubt she saw men as nothing but walking wallets to exploit. Even back in my original world, the pigs there were the same—always putting their own desires first, squealing and throwing fits whenever I did something they didn’t like, yet the moment I transferred schools or moved to the city, deciding I’d lost my use to them, not a single one came chasing after me, I say. Just look at Éclair. Show her favoritism, and she’d take it as mockery and get furious—I can picture it clearly, indeed.
“Someone like Éclair might actually make a fine pig-keeper, given how serious she is, I say.”
Éclair does seem well-suited to work as a livestock handler at a pig farm, I say.
“Don’t. Even if the Queen gave full permission, I can easily picture Eclair’s stomach developing an ulcer.”
Ren cut in here to caution me against my proposal, I say.

“True, that would be an utterly hopeless task where that princess is concerned. Considering the state of the nation and her own position, if she’d simply seduced Naofumi-san and created a fait accompli, it would’ve killed two birds with one stone—both diplomatically and politically. And yet all she managed were such short-sighted schemes.”
“Yaa… personally, I’d rather we just drop this whole topic. Even now I sometimes remember that ghostly figure of hers.”
In this world, it was the Crimson Swine who’d caused the tremendous devastation Melromarc suffered, I say. It was honestly impressive how far the country had recovered since then, indeed.
“Is the Three Heroes Church really that much of a threat? We can’t judge that for ourselves.”
“Naofumi-san burned down the church right at the start, and though it took over the country, in the end it was that princess pulling the strings behind the scenes.”
“It does seem troublesome, at least.”
Talking like this, we made our way down to the fiftieth floor.
“So, so, what’s next, I wonder.”

And… the place we emerged into looked like some kind of lake inside a dim, dusky cave, indeed. As if lying in wait, a full set of Calmar-type bosses and their escorts came out to greet us. Naturally, faced with our strength, they didn’t stand a chance and were sunk in an instant, I say.
“A full boss set from the island, all the way down here. Guess we’re getting close to the end?”
“Rather an odd combination to throw at us at this point. Maybe they figured sending them all at once would make things more troublesome?”
“Against us now, even a swarm like that isn’t much of a challenge.”
Wiped out in one sweep with an area attack, I say.
“Easy enough, but something about it feels off. So… this is an underground lake, huh?”
“…Seems like it.”
Ren, wearing a sour expression, agreed with Father’s words while turning his face toward the path that was visibly leading to the next floor, indeed.
“Let’s just hurry on ahead.”
“Now hold on—shouldn’t we investigate this blatantly suspicious lake first?”
“That was just Calmar Pengu’s battle arena. We beat them before they could even get into the water. End of discussion.”
Ren was stubbornly refusing to investigate the lake, I say. Somehow, both Itsuki and I had the feeling something was off about that, too.
“Agreed. Naofumi-san, let’s ignore Ren-san and check it out. This setup reeks of a trap.”
“Well… guess it’s gonna be me, then.”
“If something comes up, let’s stick to the plan.”
And with that, Father dove into the lake.
